flashcards.back: Creation is like an upside-down tree, rooted above in the Supreme. Ego, attachment and desire are its roots.
With the axe of Self-knowledge and detachment; then one seeks the Supreme, from which there is no return.
Those free of pride and delusion, who have conquered attachment, dwell in the Self, desires stilled, beyond pleasure and pain.
The individual soul is part of God; it gathers the six senses, mind included, and activates them.
As air carries scent from a flower, the soul carries the senses from the body it leaves to the next.

flashcards.front: Who can see the soul leave?
flashcards.back: Not the ignorant; only those with the eye of Self-knowledge.
The light of sun, moon and fire is his; he sustains beings through the earth and nourishes plants.
Memory, Self-knowledge and the removal of doubt come from him; he is known through the Vedas and is their author.
Temporal beings, which change; the eternal Spirit, which doesn't; and the Supreme, beyond both.
Because God is beyond both the temporal and the eternal.

quiz.text: What are the roots of the tree of Maya?
quiz.why: They hold beings in the world.

quiz.text: With what is the tree cut?

options.C: The axe of Self-knowledge and detachment

quiz.why: Then one reaches the goal of no return.

quiz.text: In 15.8, the soul moving to a new body is like:
quiz.why: It carries the senses with it.

quiz.text: Where does the light of sun, moon and fire come from?
quiz.why: He is the light and sustainer of all life.

quiz.text: Per 15.15, what comes from God seated in all?

options.A: Memory, knowledge and the removal of doubt

quiz.why: He is in the inner psyche of all beings.

quiz.text: Why is God called the Supreme Being (15.18)?

options.B: He is beyond both the temporal and the eternal

quiz.why: Three entities: temporal, eternal, and the Supreme beyond both.
